hook_text: Every price the state touches obeys one of two laws: pin it down, get a queue. Pin it up, get a pile.
clip_script: A school soccer tournament with no referee is not freedom — it is shin-kicking. Markets are the same game, so the state walks on with a whistle and four moves. Move one: make something dearer on purpose — tax cigarettes and sugary drinks, and less of them sells. Move two: make something cheaper on purpose — strip the VAT off brown bread, maize meal and rice while most goods carry fifteen percent. Move three: the ceiling. Pin a price down so an essential stays reachable — and at that price buyers multiply while sellers shrink back. The gap becomes a queue, then rationing, then a side door where the desperate pay more than the law allows. Ceilings make queues. Move four: the floor. Pin a price up so producers survive — and sellers pile goods high while buyers step back. Floors make piles. Put the floor under wages and you get the minimum wage: real protection for every worker who keeps a job, and — say the second half every time — a higher price on labour can mean fewer workers hired. Two truths, one instrument. That's the whole topic.
visual_style: A referee's whistle cutting to a stylised market pitch; a price bar pressed down as a queue of figures snakes off-screen and a side door glows; the bar lifted up as crates stack into a leaning tower; a wage floor holding some figures up while empty chairs fade behind them.
mood: Sharp, even-handed, revealing — consequences arriving exactly on schedule.
pacing: Brisk twin beats for tax and zero-rating, symmetrical builds for ceiling and floor, deliberate slow-down for the minimum wage's two truths.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep: the referee, the riverbank, the gate and the starting line.
